guide.title: Norwalk, Connecticut: A Rail Junction on the Sound
guide.intro: Norwalk sits where Metro-North's New Haven Line meets the Danbury Branch, which splits off at South Norwalk station on its way north — a working rail junction on Long Island Sound as much as a beach city. That harbor identity carries through its anchor institutions: the Maritime Aquarium interprets the Sound itself, the Lockwood-Mathews Mansion Museum offers guided tours of a preserved historic house, and the Norwalk Seaport Association runs seasonal cruises out to the Sheffield Island Lighthouse. Families gravitate to Stepping Stones Museum for Children in Mathews Park, while South Norwalk — known locally as SoNo — is the city's dining and entertainment neighborhood, its storefronts lining historic Washington Street. Together, these anchors make Norwalk a practical rail-accessible base for exploring the Connecticut shoreline.

sections.heading: A rail junction on the Sound
sections.body: South Norwalk station is where Metro-North's Danbury Branch splits off from the New Haven Line's main trunk — the kind of junction that has long made Norwalk a stopping-off point rather than a pass-through. That harbor identity is visible in what the city has built up around it: the Maritime Aquarium tells the story of Long Island Sound's marine life, the Lockwood-Mathews Mansion Museum preserves a historic house with guided tours, and the Norwalk Seaport Association runs seasonal cruises out to the Sheffield Island Lighthouse, including sunset trips and Tuesday clambakes in July and August. South Norwalk itself — SoNo — is Norwalk's dining and entertainment neighborhood, its storefronts still lining historic Washington Street.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Metro-North's New Haven Line serves Norwalk at South Norwalk, East Norwalk, and Rowayton stations, with the Danbury Branch diverging northward at South Norwalk — the junction station and the fastest way in from Grand Central Terminal or intermediate New Haven Line stops.

faq.question: How do I get to Norwalk?
faq.answer: Metro-North's New Haven Line stops at South Norwalk, East Norwalk, and Rowayton, with the Danbury Branch diverging northward at South Norwalk station.

faq.question: What are the Maritime Aquarium's hours?
faq.answer: Open daily, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., at 10 North Water Street in South Norwalk.

faq.question: When can I tour the Lockwood-Mathews Mansion Museum?
faq.answer: Guided tours run Wednesday through Sunday on a March-through-December schedule.

faq.question: How do I get to the Sheffield Island Lighthouse?
faq.answer: The Norwalk Seaport Association runs seasonal three-hour cruises out to the lighthouse, along with sunset cruises and Tuesday clambakes in July and August.

faq.question: Where can I stay in Norwalk?
faq.answer: The Watershed, part of the Hotel Zero Degrees/RMS hotel family, is Norwalk's verified in-town lodging option.
